content.question_text: What exactly is an enumerated type in Java?

core_requirements: It is a class that has a fixed number of predefined instances.
The instances are declared inside the enum declaration (the constants).
acceptable_variations: A class with a fixed set of constants.
A type with a limited set of predefined values.

content.question_text: How do you refer to an enumerated constant?

core_requirements: Using the class name followed by the constant: ClassName.CONSTANT

content.question_text: In what three situations can you use the simple name of an enumerated constant (without the class prefix)?

core_requirements: Inside methods of the enumeration itself.
In a case of a switch statement/expression when the selector has the enum type.
When you statically import all constants of the enumeration.
acceptable_variations: Inside enum methods, in switch cases, and with static import.

content.question_text: Can you statically import constants from an enumeration that is in the default package?

core_requirements: No.
You cannot statically import constants from an enumeration in the default package.

content.question_text: Can you construct a new object of an enumerated type that is different from the ones declared in the enum?

core_requirements: No.
It is not possible to construct new objects beyond the declared constants.

content.question_text: How should you compare values of enumerated types?

core_requirements: Use == (the equality operator).
You never need to use .equals() for enum values because there are only a fixed number of instances.

content.question_text: Of which class are all enumerated types subclasses?

core_requirements: The Enum class (java.lang.Enum).

content.question_text: What useful methods do enumerated types inherit from the Enum class?

core_requirements: name() — returns the name of the enumerated constant.
ordinal() — returns the position (zero-based) of the constant in the declaration.
valueOf() — returns the constant with the given name (static method).

content.question_text: What does the name() method do for an enumerated type?

core_requirements: It returns the name of the enumerated constant as a String.
acceptable_variations: It returns the constant's declared name.

content.question_text: What does the values() method do for an enumerated type?

core_requirements: It returns an array containing all the constants of the enumeration in the order they were declared.
acceptable_variations: It returns an array of all enum values.

content.question_text: What does the ordinal() method do for an enumerated type?

core_requirements: It returns the position of the enumerated constant in the enum declaration.
The position is zero-based (the first constant has ordinal 0).
acceptable_variations: Returns the index/position of the constant.
Zero-based position in the declaration order.

content.question_text: Can enumerations have fields and methods?

core_requirements: Yes.
You can add constructors, methods, and fields to an enumerated type.

content.question_text: Why can you omit the private modifier on an enum constructor?

core_requirements: The constructor of an enumeration is always private by default.
It is a syntax error to declare an enum constructor as public or protected.

content.question_text: What are enums meant to represent?

core_requirements: A fixed set of constants.
acceptable_variations: A fixed set of predefined values.
A limited set of constant values.

content.question_text: Can an enum with no instances be instantiated?

core_requirements: No.
An enumeration with no instances cannot be instantiated.

content.question_text: What are enums with no instances useful for, and why?

core_requirements: They are useful for utility classes that only contain static methods.
Because they cannot be instantiated (no instances), they act like a class with a private constructor.
acceptable_variations: For utility classes with only static methods.
As a utility class alternative since they cannot be instantiated.
